data.analysis: Choose N=3: the baseline exposes three complementary opportunities—parallelizing independent cells, improving the single-step kernel, and reusing data across timesteps. A fourth arithmetic-only track would substantially overlap the kernel work. The supplied valid baseline runs six serial stencil sweeps and does not use its `threads` argument. Its three recorded times are 0.4606, 0.4458, and 0.4661 s (mean 0.4575 s); no candidate comparisons or per-thread-count breakdown are supplied. Keep the baseline as G until measured programs are available. All trees must preserve both full output buffers, the six-step parity and boundary behavior, the supplied tolerance, and the `threads` CPU budget for all valid inputs. Compare correct candidates under the frozen protocol at one and four cores; do not assume gains combine. Later independently confirm the integrated G on the separate confirmation seeds. The GCC optimization-options reference consulted is publisher-current rather than verified as GCC 14.2, so it motivates checking measured vectorization only—not assuming particular compiler flags or generated instructions.

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, explore OpenMP decomposition of the independent stencil cells, using no more than the `threads` budget and preserving a synchronization point between timesteps. Compare a persistent parallel region with suitable static spatial partitioning against the serial path, including one-thread overhead. Keep SIMD and multi-timestep fusion out of scope to isolate thread-level effects. Verify correctness on smaller checks and n=256, then measure at one and four cores.
children.subject: OpenMP parallelization and thread-budget scaling

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, optimize the single-timestep stencil kernel around contiguous x traversal: investigate compiler vectorization or supported x86 SIMD, reduced indexing overhead, and reuse/unrolling of the radius-1-to-3 taps. Do not assume an ISA extension or alignment for the interior rows beyond the frozen build and stated input alignment. Preserve numerical tolerance and boundaries; avoid adding threading or temporal fusion so the kernel effect can be measured independently. Validate and measure both official core settings.
children.subject: Contiguous-x SIMD and single-step kernel efficiency

children.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, investigate spatial/temporal cache blocking that fuses multiple consecutive timesteps per tile, accounting for the radius-3 halo at each step and the alternating even/odd buffers. Any scratch allocation is timed; preserve initialization and all untouched boundary values, and compare against the unfused serial baseline without assuming fusion is beneficial. Keep explicit thread parallelization and SIMD changes out of scope to isolate data-reuse effects. Validate on smaller checks and n=256, then measure at one and four cores.
children.subject: Cache reuse through halo-correct temporal blocking
